figure_caption: Protocol overview. An anonymised comparison table is fit with a ridge-penalised Bradley–Terry model; a target adjacent pair (top or mid) is selected; a removal search proposes at most 2% of rows; the evaluator deletes them, refits exactly, tests whether the pair reverses, and records the verified budget k and score 1 − k/k_cap. Random, influence-only and opponent-targeted removal serve as comparators; empty-set, label-permutation and cross-table copy runs serve as controls. The search stage scored configurations on crowd-vote and expert-judgment development tables; one frozen configuration was then evaluated once in the sealed final stage on crowd-vote and sports held-out tables. The two stages are kept separate.

panels.title: Removal protocol
panels.short_caption: Delete rows, refit exactly, test whether the adjacent pair reverses; search, baselines and controls share one evaluator.
panels.drawio_prompt:
SINGLE IDEA: one picture of the studied perturbation loop — delete comparisons, refit exactly, test whether an adjacent pair reverses — with the removal-search instrument, three baselines and three controls all plugging into the same evaluator.

NODES (stable IDs, semantic encoding):
- T (data table, sharp box with small row-grid glyph): 'Comparison table' with sub-label '$$N$$ rows, anonymised'.
- FIT0 (rounded process box): 'Ridge BT fit'.
- LB (small ranked list glyph, 5 stacked bars, adjacent pair of bars h above l highlighted by a bracket): 'Leaderboard'.
- PAIR (rounded box): 'Target adjacent pair' with two tiny tags 'Top' and 'Mid' (top = ranks 1–2, mid = middle ranks).
- SEARCH (large grouped container, rounded, titled 'Removal search'): holds three small rounded sub-steps in a left-to-right chain: S1 'Influence order' (sub-label 'prefix bisection'), S2 'Re-linearised greedy', S3 'Drop-and-readd polish'. A tiny 'exact refit at each probe' tag sits on S1. Container output node RSET (data, sharp box): 'Removal set $$R$$', with a cap badge '$$|R|\le k_{cap}$$ = 2% of rows'.
- DEL (rounded process box): 'Delete rows $$R$$'.
- FIT1 (rounded process box): 'Exact refit' (same objective).
- FLIP (diamond decision): 'Pair reverses?' with exit labels 'yes' and 'no'.
- OUT (sharp result box, emphasized): 'Verified budget $$k$$' with small sub-label 'score $$1-k/k_{cap}$$'.
- Evaluator boundary: a dashed rounded frame labelled 'Evaluator' enclosing DEL, FIT1, FLIP, OUT (the evaluator, not the search, owns the refit and the verification).
- BASE (grouped container titled 'Baselines', three stacked small rounded boxes): B1 'Random removal', B2 'Influence only', B3 'Opponent-targeted'. Each acts as an alternative proposer of a removal set.
- CTRL (grouped container titled 'Controls', three stacked small rounded boxes): C1 'Empty set', C2 'Label permutation', C3 'Cross-table copy'. Each is a validity check expected NOT to flip.

EDGES (source → target, style, label):
- T → FIT0 solid, no label.
- FIT0 → LB solid, label '$$\theta$$ ranks'.
- LB → PAIR solid, no label.
- T → SEARCH solid (data input), no label (route along the top).
- PAIR → SEARCH solid, label 'target'.
- S1 → S2 solid; S2 → S3 solid; S3 → RSET solid (inside/exit of container).
- RSET → DEL solid, label 'proposes ≤ 2%'.
- BASE → DEL solid, drawn as a bracket/merge arrow into DEL, label 'alternative proposers'.
- CTRL → DEL solid, drawn as a second bracket/merge arrow into DEL, label 'sanity runs'; the CTRL edge and the BASE edge take distinct edge colors.
- DEL → FIT1 solid, no label.
- FIT1 → FLIP solid, no label.
- FLIP → OUT solid, label 'yes'.
- FLIP → RSET dashed (feedback / auxiliary), label 'no: search again' routed back below the evaluator frame.
- T → DEL dashed thin, label 'remaining rows' (the table minus deleted rows feeds the refit): draw as dashed edge from T to FIT1 along the bottom.

SPATIAL LAYOUT (left-to-right, panel is about 1.2:1 landscape, half the figure width): Column 1 (far left, stacked vertically): T on top, FIT0 below it, LB below that, PAIR at the bottom — read as a short vertical chain. Column 2–3 (centre): SEARCH container as a wide horizontal band at the upper centre with S1→S2→S3 inside. Below SEARCH, stacked: BASE (left) and CTRL (right) side by side at the lower centre. Column 4 (right): the Evaluator frame, with DEL on top, FIT1 below it, FLIP diamond below it, and OUT at the bottom-right, flowing top to bottom. BASE and CTRL merge-arrows enter DEL together with RSET.

IMPORTANCE RANKING: (1) FLIP + OUT (the reversal test and verified budget k), (2) DEL → FIT1 loop inside Evaluator frame, (3) SEARCH container, (4) PAIR/LB, (5) BASE and CTRL, (6) T and FIT0. Make SEARCH visibly the studied instrument versus BASE as comparators and CTRL as checks.

panels.title: Search versus sealed final stage
panels.short_caption: Two stages, two designs each: search on crowd votes and expert judgments; sealed final on crowd votes and sports.
panels.drawio_prompt:
SINGLE IDEA: the evaluation is split into two sealed-apart stages, each measuring two designs — the search stage (crowd votes + expert judgments) selects a configuration, and the sealed final stage (crowd votes + sports) evaluates that one frozen configuration once.

NODES (stable IDs, semantic encoding):
- STAGE_S (large rounded container, titled 'Search stage'): holds two data-table nodes (sharp boxes with small grid glyph): DS_CROWD 'Crowd votes' with sub-label 'Arena 55k', and DS_EXPERT 'Expert judgments' with sub-label 'MT-Bench human'. Each table carries two small tags 'Top' and 'Mid' (the two target pairs). Also inside: CFG (rounded process box): 'Search configurations' (a stack of three small offset cards to show several candidates) and a small badge 'Seeds 11, 12'.
- PICK (rounded process box between stages): 'Freeze one configuration'.
- STAGE_F (large rounded container, titled 'Sealed final stage'): holds DF_CROWD 'Crowd votes' with sub-label 'Arena 140k, deduplicated', and DF_SPORT 'Sports' with sub-label 'NBA games'. Each table carries tags 'Top' and 'Mid'. Also inside: FROZEN (rounded process box with a lock glyph, frozen = not trainable/not modified): 'Frozen configuration', evaluated once, and a small badge 'Seeds 21, 22'.
- SEP (a thick dashed vertical/horizontal barrier line between the two containers, labelled 'never combined').
- SHARED marker: DS_CROWD and DF_CROWD both carry a small matching 'crowd-vote design' bracket-glyph or identical icon to show the same design appears in both stages with different tables; DS_EXPERT has an icon unique to the search stage, DF_SPORT has an icon unique to the final stage.

EDGES (source → target, style, label):
- DS_CROWD → CFG solid, no label; DS_EXPERT → CFG solid, no label (tables are scored by configurations).
- CFG → PICK solid, label 'scores'.
- PICK → FROZEN solid, label 'frozen' (crosses the SEP barrier).
- FROZEN → DF_CROWD solid; FROZEN → DF_SPORT solid, no labels (one pass, evaluated once).
- DS_CROWD ↔ DF_CROWD dashed thin double-headed, label 'same design' (auxiliary; keep very light).

SPATIAL LAYOUT: stack vertically (panel is about 1.2:1 landscape; keep it compact and centered, using the width for the two side-by-side tables per container): Search stage container on top, PICK and SEP barrier in the middle, Sealed final stage container at the bottom. Within each container: the two data tables side by side at the container's top, the configuration/frozen box below them. Align DS_CROWD directly above DF_CROWD so the 'same design' dashed link is a short vertical line.

IMPORTANCE RANKING: (1) the two stage containers and the SEP barrier, (2) the four table nodes with their designs, (3) PICK / FROZEN, (4) seeds badges, (5) the 'same design' link.
